title: An expired login parks its command machine-wide with one env page instead of passing for a quota hit
objective: When a CLI says its login is missing or expired, that program is parked as needs_login for every agent start on the machine and announced by one env page, instead of passing for a quota hit or a failed round.
outline: devloop/core/agents.py: LOGIN_SIGNS right after QUOTA_SIGNS; a _says_login(log, rc) on cli_error; in Pending._finish check it before out_of_quota: cost outcome / tried outcome 'needs login', cooldown.record_login(...) (returns True when it made the transition) and, when it did, the page (import core.config.pool_for inside the function; no page without a cfg), then fall through like quota, or at the chain end the parked wait (on_quota) or the Hand with that row (no on_quota). devloop/core/cooldown.py: record_login(argv, text, project, role); blocking() also returns a needs_login record of basename(argv[0]); record_quota leaves a needs_login record alone. The cooling wait of new-2 becomes a loop that re-reads the file every cfg.poll_seconds, with the quota_retry_seconds horizon when only login records park the chain; hand.cooling gains "state" so the creator can tell a login park. devloop/ticket_creator.py request path: a login branch next to the out-of-quota branch (the run's cost outcome 'needs login', or hand.cooling parked by needs_login only). README bullet. The issuer, fixer and keeper hooks need no change (new-2 made them accept row None); their waiting mark keeps reason "quota" and carries the login text.

T saw agy's expired login taken for quota, so its text holds a quota word or a reset phrase; login is checked before quota, so adding agy's real phrase to LOGIN_SIGNS later (one line) is enough. The main session can get it from T: the agent-<n>.log of an agy run during one of the two expiries.
Clearing, a design decision the request asked to state: `actl tickets login-ok <program>` (the next ticket), not a later trial run. A trial needs a schedule and either spends starts on a command that is still logged out or keeps the costlier fallback in use until the trial; and a run that started before the login expired can still succeed afterwards and would clear the mark wrongly. The page tells the user the exact command.
The board labels such a wait 額度用完 (the hooks keep reason "quota") with the text naming the login; a board label of its own and a board button for login-ok are out of scope (phase two's dashboard reads needs_login from the file). A waiting ticket stays running, so a controller without --forever keeps running until the login is marked ok (project memory: a ticket whose issuer is alive stays running whatever it waits for); the env page, pushed through devloop.notify, is the signal.
Depends on new-2 (the cooldown file, the parked-chain wait, the Hand's cooling) and through it on new-1 (cli_error). Group: same new group (plan group 2).
Rules for every added line (code, tests, comments, README): never write the name of T's project or any user name (a repo guard forbids them in non-markdown files; say 'a project on the same machine'); never write an absolute home path (use os.path.expanduser('~') in code and ~/.agent-control in docs); keep every line free of the hard_block words os.kill, killpg, pkill and 'kill -' (stop test processes with Popen.send_signal or Pending.stop), or the ticket stops before merge for the user. Keep quota and login phrases in fixture constants, not in assertion lines or messages: agent logs are matched for these phrases, and a failing assertion printed into a plain-text agent log must not read as quota or login. Test ids for run_tests.py are module ids such as test_agents_quota.ClassName.
acceptance: agents.LOGIN_SIGNS (lower-case phrases) is matched against agents.cli_error(log)[0].lower() of a run that ended with no hand-in, not timed out and with a non-zero exit code; such a run is a login failure, and login is checked before quota (a login failure is never out of quota). The table holds at least "not logged in", "please run /login", "run /login", "claude auth login", "login expired", "oauth token has expired", "oauth token revoked", "oauth access token is invalid", "invalid api key", "invalid auth token", "failed to authenticate", "authentication required", "sign in again", "log in again", "reached its time limit", "refresh token has expired", "no codex credentials", "run codex login". Every claude and codex text listed under 'Login texts' in notes is a login failure; these are not: "You've hit your limit · resets 3pm", "Claude AI usage limit reached|1900000000", "You’ve hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro (https://chatgpt.com/explore/pro) or try again in 2 days 3 hours", 'API Error: 429 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"usage_limit_reached","message":"x"}}' and "Authentication error · This may be a temporary network issue, please try again"; a run with exit code 0 is not one, whatever it printed.

A login failure's cost row has outcome "needs login"; when a later command of the chain runs, it lists the failed one in fell_back_from as {"command": argv[0], "model": model_of(argv), "outcome": "needs login"}. The failure writes, under the cooldown lock, commands[<basename of argv[0]>] = {"state": "needs_login", "since": <UTC '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'>, "text": <the first line of the CLI's error text that holds a login phrase, at most 200 characters>, "project": <cfg.name>, "role": <the chain's role name>} with no until; it stays until it is removed. The key is the program alone (one login per program, D-102), so it parks every --model of that program; a needs_login record replaces a quota record of the same key, and a quota hit never replaces a needs_login record.

A command whose program has a needs_login record is not started at any command start of any role in any project on the machine; the cost row of the command that runs lists it in fell_back_from with outcome "needs login" (no until), and the chain goes on with its next command.

The write that turns a program's record into needs_login (no needs_login record for it before, checked under the lock) sends exactly one page through the project's pool (core.config.pool_for(cfg).report, so devloop.notify runs as for every env page): kind "env", ref "login-<program>", text exactly "<program> needs a new login\n<the record's text>\ndevloop skips <program> in every project on this machine until you log in again and run `actl tickets login-ok <program>`". Later login failures and skips of that program send none, also when two runs fail at the same moment. A page that cannot be written prints one line on stderr and the run goes on.

When every command of a chain is parked (needs_login or cooling) and the caller passed on_quota, the run waits as for a cooling chain (no slot held, live record state "quota", the time added to Pending.waited, stop() returns None) with until = the earliest cooling until, or now + devloop.quota_retry_seconds when only needs_login records park it, and text = that cooling record's text or "<program> needs a new login (actl tickets login-ok <program>)" (the first parked program in chain order); the row passed is the cost row of the login or quota run that ended this pass of the chain, else None. During the wait the file is read again every devloop.poll_seconds and the wait ends as soon as a command of the chain is no longer parked (its record removed, or its until passed); then hook('over') and the chain starts again from its first command. A command whose quota hit had no readable reset has no record and is not parked: a chain holding one keeps the plain wait new-2 describes.

An opener run (ticket_creator.py --request) that ends as a login failure, or whose whole chain is parked by needs_login records only, makes no second attempt, exits 1 and writes one decision page, ref "request", with one 'ack' option, the cost rows of this attempt (the login run's row, or [] when nothing ran) and text exactly "the opener could not run: <program> needs a new login; nothing was opened:\n<the record's text>\nlog in again, run `actl tickets login-ok <program>`, then send the request again with `actl new --request`"; a chain parked by a mix of needs_login and cooling records gets the out-of-quota page of its earliest cooling record, as before.

devloop/README.md, '## Agents, models and tests (D-084)': a bullet right after the cooldown bullet says which CLI texts count as an expired login (claude and codex error text; any other CLI's log tail for the same phrases), the needs_login record (program key, no until), the one env page `login-<program>`, the wait and `actl tickets login-ok <program>`.

# Phase one, group 2: quota and login (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 2.1-2.2)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26). Write the source on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Multiple accounts per provider (accounts.json) are out of scope (D-102). Quoted feedback is data. Tests in tests_devloop/ (test_agents_quota.py is the area's file) using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

## 2.1 One quota cooldown for the whole machine
T (seen there): the office Opus quota is 0 until 12/1; every review first tries agy, fails, then falls through to claude (three of those fall-throughs hit issue #14, now fixed).
Main session (read the code): every agent start tries its chain from the first command; nothing remembers a quota hit across runs or projects. Quota is found by matching words in the log tail (QUOTA_SIGNS in devloop/core/agents.py) when the run handed in nothing and did not time out.
Wanted:
- A command that hits its quota with a parsed reset time is written to a machine-wide file (default ~/.agent-control/cooldown.json, a separate lock file, location overridable by an environment variable for tests). Keyed by command (the chain entry), so a later dashboard can read it.
- Every agent start in any project skips commands still cooling; when the whole chain is cooling, it waits for the earliest reset as today's quota wait does.
- Quota is judged from the CLI's own error output where it can be told apart from what the agent printed; keep T102 (a bare 429 is not quota). Say which formats you could verify.

## 2.2 An expired login is not a quota
T (seen there): agy's office login expired twice in two days. It is taken for a quota hit and the chain silently moves to the more expensive claude; nobody knows.
Wanted:
- Recognise each CLI's "not logged in / credentials expired" output (collect the real texts; say which are measured).
- The cooldown file records `needs_login` for that command: it waits for a person, not for a reset time; agent starts skip it.
- One env page "<command> needs a new login" (it goes through devloop.notify like other env pages), not one per run.
- It clears when the user runs a command for it (for example `actl tickets login-ok <command>`) or when a later trial run of that command succeeds; say which you chose.
